```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE, error = FALSE)
project <- Sys.glob("projects/tanaka_*")
project <- project[file.exists(file.path(project, "analysis", "candidates.R"))]
stopifnot(length(project) == 1L)
source(file.path(project, "analysis/derive_cohort.R"))
# pandoc はパイプ表の区切り線（|---|）の長さの比で docx の列幅を決める。knitr は区切り線を各列の
# 最長の中身の長さにするので、長い説明の列があると数値の列が細くなり、Word や Google ドキュメントで
# 「46」が「4/6」のように折り返す。区切り線の長さを、各列の最長の中身に余白の3字を足した値（上限18字）、
# ただし最長の単語＋余白より狭くしない値に置き換える。
fix_pipe_widths <- function(k) {
  lines <- as.character(k)
  sep <- grep("^\\|[|: -]+\\|$", lines)[1]
  if (is.na(sep)) return(k)
  cells <- function(line) trimws(strsplit(sub("^\\|", "", sub("\\|$", "", line)), "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  rows <- lapply(lines[-sep], cells)
  n_col <- length(cells(lines[sep]))
  rows <- rows[vapply(rows, length, 1L) == n_col]
  col_text <- lapply(seq_len(n_col), function(j) vapply(rows, `[`, "", j))
  longest <- vapply(col_text, function(x) max(nchar(x, type = "width")), 1)
  longest_word <- vapply(col_text, function(x) max(nchar(unlist(strsplit(x, "\\s+")), type = "width"), 0), 1)
  # +3 はセルの内側の余白の分。長い説明は単語の切れ目で折り返してよいが、1語の名前や数字は割らない。
  width <- pmax(pmin(longest + 3, 18), longest_word + 3, 8)
  # 区切り線の合計が pandoc の行幅（72字）に満たないと、表がその割合だけ狭くなる。比率を保って引き伸ばす。
  if (sum(width) < 80) width <- ceiling(width * 80 / sum(width))
  align <- cells(lines[sep])
  lines[sep] <- paste0("|", paste(vapply(seq_len(n_col), function(j) {
    a <- align[j]
    paste0(if (startsWith(a, ":")) ":" else "-", strrep("-", width[j] - 2), if (endsWith(a, ":")) ":" else "-")
  }, ""), collapse = "|"), "|")
  knitr::asis_output(paste0("\n", paste(lines, collapse = "\n"), "\n"))
}
pipe_tab <- function(x) {
  fix_pipe_widths(knitr::kable(x, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE))
}
# パイプ表への変換で gtsummary の字下げ（行頭の空白）が落ち、変数名と水準が同じ位置に並ぶ。
# 水準の行の先頭にノーブレークスペースを入れ、変数名の行を太字にして上下関係を残す。
gts_pipe <- function(tbl) {
  tbl <- gtsummary::modify_table_body(tbl, function(body) {
    body$label <- ifelse(body$row_type == "label", body$label, paste0(strrep(" ", 4), body$label))
    body
  })
  fix_pipe_widths(gtsummary::as_kable(gtsummary::bold_labels(tbl), format = "pipe"))
}
```

if (FALLBACK) {
  cat("**WARNING: this report was built on the synthetic 100-row data with substitute candidates. ",
      "The records carry no real stroke or incident content, so every number below is meaningless.**\n\n", sep = "")
}

## Summary

This report describes aspiration and choking incidents that occurred during food or fluid intake in
stroke inpatients, using the Safe Master incident-report data (version r19, reports from 2013 to 2024,
`r fmt_n(flow$all)` reports). Keyword search identified `r flow$candidates` candidate reports among
`r fmt_n(flow$inpatient)` inpatient reports. At stage 1, two reviewers independently judged eligibility for all `r flow$candidates` candidates in a web
application, with disagreements resolved by consensus; `r flow$excluded_stage1` candidates were excluded.
At stage 2, two reviewers independently classified a random pilot sample of `r n_pilot` eligible reports,
resolved disagreements by consensus, and revised the classification criteria. For the remaining
`r n_rest_review` reports, one reviewer checked AI drafts generated by Claude using majority voting across
three independent runs. During this review, `r flow$excluded_stage2` reports were found ineligible and
excluded; in the `r n_rest_review - flow$excluded_stage2` retained reports, the reviewer changed or filled
`r n_review_changed` of `r n_review_items` classification items. The final cohort comprises `r n_cohort` reports
(`r flow$excluded` candidates were excluded across both stages). `r n_severe` reports (`r sprintf("%.0f", sev_pct)`%)
met the severe-outcome definition, and `r n_death` reports described a death. The analysis is purely descriptive:
no regression was fitted and no p-values are given.

## Table 1. Characteristics overall and by severity

```{r table1}
gts_pipe(tbl1)
```

Values are n (%) of reports in the column. Patient age is a coded 10-year category, not an age in years.
Patient-state items are checkbox fields: a blank cannot be told apart from "not recorded", so unmarked items
are counted as not marked. No p-values are presented.

## Table 1b. Characteristics overall and by the role of stroke in the admission

```{r table1b}
gts_pipe(tbl1b)
```

The same characteristics as Table 1, in columns by the role of stroke in the admission (the column headings
carry the stratum names). Values are n (%) of reports in the column. No p-values are presented.

## Table 2. Feeding assistance and presence of others, by event type and by the role of stroke

```{r table2}
pipe_tab(table2)
```

The "Stratified by" column names the stratification: overall, event type, or the role of stroke in the admission
(primary condition, managed sequela or comorbidity or history, unclear). Severe % is severe n divided by n of the row. Unknown is an explicit level. Strata with small n should be read as descriptive only.

## Table 3. Severe proportion with exact 95% confidence intervals

```{r table3}
pipe_tab(table3)
```

`Severe/N` shows the numerator and denominator so that small cells are visible; no cell is suppressed.
The 95% confidence intervals are exact (Clopper--Pearson). The assistance-by-presence rows include only
cases in which both items were determinable.

## Figure 2. Reports and severe proportion by feeding assistance and presence of others

```{r fig2, fig.width=8, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Figure 2. Number of reports (light bar) and severe reports (dark bar) by feeding assistance and presence of others, in panels by the role of stroke in the admission."}
print(fig2)
```

## Table S1. Severe outcome under alternative definitions

```{r tables1}
pipe_tab(table_s1)
```

## Table S2. Agreement between the two reviewers

```{r tables2}
pipe_tab(table_s2)
```

Agreement is for candidates both reviewers judged. For classification items, n is the number of candidates
both reviewers included; rescue intervention is limited to candidates both reviewers classed as choking.
Kappa is unweighted, with an asymptotic 95% confidence interval; a dash means the table is degenerate.

```{r determinable}
if (!is.null(determinable)) {
  pipe_tab(data.frame(Variable = determinable$variable, Reviewer = determinable$reviewer, n = determinable$n,
                      `Determinable n` = determinable$n_determinable,
                      `Determinable, %` = ifelse(is.na(determinable$proportion), "-", sprintf("%.0f", determinable$proportion)),
                      check.names = FALSE))
}
```

Determinable means the item was not judged unknown by that reviewer, among candidates both reviewers included.

## Table S3. Swallowing assessment, instruction deviation, meal, rescue intervention, and direct assistant

```{r tables3}
pipe_tab(table_s3)
```

The direct assistant is described only for reports in which the reviewers identified a single involved staff
member (`r n_party_identified` of `r n_cohort`). Experience and time in the department are the years column times 12 plus the months column (0--11).

## Table S4. Reasons for exclusion on review

```{r tables4}
pipe_tab(table_s4)
```

## Notes

- **Severe outcome.** Severe means injury severity "death", or injury severity "possible residual disability (high or low)"
  together with an intensive treatment. Death is always counted as severe, even without an intensive treatment.
- **Sensitivity definitions.** Table S1 gives two wider definitions; they are not used in the main tables.
- **Candidate selection.** Candidates were selected by keywords and codes, then judged by two reviewers without any AI-generated draft.
  Reports that were never retrieved by the keywords are not part of the cohort.
- **Reporting.** Reports come from institutions required to report and from voluntary participants; the numbers describe the composition of the reports received and are not incidence or risk.
- **Statistics.** No p-values were computed and no regression was fitted.
